newsitem.title: UK: Is your dog immature? Blame breeding.
newsitem.headline: Is your dog immature? Blame breeding.

text.p: Dogs that act like big, silly puppies their whole lives have a good excuse -- they were bred to be that way, British researchers reported on Thursday.
The less a dog looks like its ancestor the wolf, the more likely it is to display "immature" canine behaviour, John Bradshaw of Southampton University and colleagues found.
According to New Scientist magazine, they tested 10 different breeds of dog and compared their behaviour to standard wolf behaviour.
Some -- especially German Shepherds and Siberian huskies -- acted a lot like wolves with growling and aggressive attitudes.
But others, like the King Charles spaniel, acted like wolf puppies their whole lives.
Bradshaw said physical and perhaps behavioural immaturity had been bred into dogs for thousands of years.
"If you look at the skull structure of a Pekinese, it's a foetus," he said.

This could explain why toy dogs were so anxious when left alone. "These juvenile types have a problem with separation anxiety," said Donna Brander, a pet behaviour counsellor at the Royal College of Veterinary Medicine in Edinburgh. "They have never gone into a more mature mode of behaviour."
